decision_points.requirement: A peer KeyPackage claim requires both the participant authorization and the outer service authorization; either one missing or invalid fails closed, and the device and Agent signer-evidence branches are an exact XOR that cannot fall back to one another.

The participant signature binds the exact unsigned request together with the source and destination service identity, so a valid authorization cannot be forwarded to another destination or deployment.

The destination independently enforces both directional Contact heads and scopes, the capability gate and the requester authority without consulting Consent, and business failures expose neither target inventory nor per-device reasons while leaving KeyPackage state unchanged.

Every claim record carries the accepted authorization Event id of its own closed branch as an exact XOR of the device and Agent forms; a record with neither, with both, or naming another accepted Event is rejected.

The unique producer proof is verifiable from the authorization Event envelope and its portable signer evidence alone; a proof that can only be checked by replaying the producer's control history, or whose signer evidence resolves to a superseded key, does not satisfy the requirement.

The destination-signed claim_receipt is verified over the claim bytes the requester recomputes rather than over any reserialization carried in the response, and its claim_request_id is the request's own value.

The requester checks the authorization Event embedded signer evidence, the claim receipt, the KeyPackage signature and every selector before installing a KeyPackage or authoring a Welcome, and any single mismatch blocks both.
The wire carries no PCR, control-history, device or Agent signer-evidence sidecar, and an external verifier never replays PCR genesis, RealmCommits or complete control history.

The signed MlsWelcomeDelivery keypackage_claim_ref resolves the exact durable claim record; the recipient recomputes the KeyPackage digest from those claimed bytes before decrypting. The delivery has no duplicated digest or Event payload.

The recipient checks the signed LeafNode capability set in the exact claimed KeyPackage against group requirements before decrypting; a mismatch is rejected without relying on a duplicated Welcome capability digest.

The recipient runtime checks the accepted winning Add Commit for that Welcome on the same accepted Genesis lineage; a Welcome with no accepted Add Commit, one matching a losing Commit of the same epoch, or one whose Commit was accepted on another lineage is rejected.

The signed delivery, durable claim ledger and accepted winning Add Commit agree on requester, recipient endpoint, KeyPackage claim, group and epoch; a mismatch or unverified local cache entry rejects before decrypting.

The original claim is consumed only after the Welcome is processed and the group state is durably stored; a failed durable store produces no recipient receipt, the peer surface offers no consume proxy, and an indeterminate result is recovered by replaying the same signed request rather than by rotating the claim identity or claiming a replacement in parallel.
Only an active mls-ciphersuite-registry row reaches KeyPackage or Commit wire; unknown and reserved rows are rejected without a state change.
Publish, claim and Commit submission independently reject an unregistered or inactive ciphersuite with no partial write.
A receiver neither tries a sequence until one suite succeeds nor rewrites a foreign suite identifier into the active identifier.
The claim, Welcome delivery and RFC 9420 BasicCredential preserve the same complete ActorId rather than a principal, DID, device id or handle projection.

cases.name: group_capability_floor
assertions: the outer KeyPackage record capabilities exactly equal the signed LeafNode keypackage_capabilities extension
every Add and Update leaf supports every current required_keypackage_capabilities value
the RFC 9420 required_capabilities extension requires support for 0xF1C0, 0xF1C1 and 0xF1C2
a sender uses a content or policy profile only when its registered capability is in the current group floor

cases.name: exhaustion_claim_limits
assertions: the local inventory ledger emits one bounded deficit batch without a remote inventory probe
claim attempts above 5 per requester/target tuple in 60 seconds fail without target enumeration
the audit reason for rate limiting is keypackage_claim_rate_limited
expired claimed KeyPackages become revoked or unusable and late consume is rejected
published to revoked with principal_deactivated reason is constructible for account deactivation
expired is not a KeyPackage lifecycle wire state and must fail schema validation

cases.name: last_resort_claim_and_reuse
assertions: single-use KeyPackages are preferred while available
last-resort KeyPackages are returned only after the single-use pool is empty
last-resort claim records carry last_resort=true
last-resort consume is idempotent and does not transition the package to consumed
each consume emits an independent append-only audit record

cases.name: last_resort_forced_rotation
assertions: when the holder comes online, the old last-resort package is rotated out
new claims receive the replacement last-resort KeyPackage
every group joined through the old last-resort package gets an MLS self-update Commit

Future epoch confidentiality requires an effective secret update unknown to the attacker and the applicable MLS recovery conditions; rotation and expiry do not restore confidentiality of captured old Welcome ciphertext.

cases.name: last_resort_affinity_and_optionality
assertions: last-resort KeyPackages are reusable only inside their intended_realm_id
cross-Realm reuse fails with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation
servers that do not advertise the feature must not return last_resort=true packages
a missing Realm-local last-resort entry fails closed instead of reusing another Realm's package
high-security and sovereign Realms forbid ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1 and fail closed on last_resort=true claim records

cases.name: peer_claim_atomic_idempotency
assertions: claim ledger uniqueness is scoped by source_id and claim_request_id
claim_envelope signing input binds claim_receipt.claim_request_id as claim_request_id without duplicating it in the envelope wire
claim CAS, target portable evidence and the serialized success outcome commit at one linearization boundary
an uncertain caller queries the original request instead of issuing a fresh claim
same request id with another canonical digest cannot mutate KeyPackage state
exact replay and query return byte-identical target evidence rather than regenerating it against a later authority snapshot
a genuinely new claim attempt uses a newly generated claim_request_id

cases.name: self_claim_authorization_idempotency
assertions: local and remote claims use the same unsigned request, authorization and transport-binding transcript
the authorization signer is the requester's accepted current-generation device method
the device authorization Event and model generation are replay-verified before accepting the authorization
participant authorization is independent of sender-constrained service transport authentication and target policy
claim CAS, claim_request_id ledger and serialized outcome commit at one linearization boundary
same identity and digest replay returns the original outcome without selecting another package
conflicting identity reuse fails before target inventory lookup

cases.name: peer_claim_double_authorization_privacy
assertions: participant authorization and outer service authorization are both mandatory
the participant signature binds the exact request and service/trust-domain destination
the destination independently enforces both directional Contact heads/scopes, capability and authority gates without consulting Consent
Direct Conversation peer claim never falls back to a last-resort KeyPackage
business failures do not expose target inventory or per-device reasons
claims_digest and the destination receipt cover returned evidence bytes but never replace the underlying identity-root, RealmCommit and current-authority verification
device and Agent evidence branches are exact XOR and cannot fall back to one another

cases.name: welcome_keypackage_hash
assertions: the closed MlsWelcomeDelivery carries one typed keypackage_claim_ref, producer proof and exact ciphertext; it is not an Event payload
recipient resolves the exact durable claim ledger entry by keypackage_claim_ref and recomputes the KeyPackage digest from the claimed bytes before decrypting
a mismatched digest or claim binding rejects the delivery before decryption; the delivery has no duplicated claim_ref digest field

cases.name: welcome_capabilities_digest_mismatch
assertions: the recipient rechecks required capabilities against the claimed signed LeafNode and exact claim ledger entry before decrypting
a capability mismatch rejects before decryption; the delivery does not carry a duplicate capabilities digest

cases.name: last_resort_expiry_blocks_new_claim_not_old_decryption
assertions: Station MUST reject a new claim for an expired last-resort package
An attacker with captured Welcome ciphertext and the matching compromised key can recover its encrypted GroupSecrets after expiry
A subsequent effective secret update cannot retroactively restore old Welcome confidentiality

cases.name: peer_claim_response_verification_before_install

claim_receipt.covered_input: the exact claim bytes of this keypackage_claim_record

assertions: the claim record carries the accepted authorization Event id of its own closed branch, and the device and Agent ids are an exact XOR rather than two optional members

on the device branch the requester Station obtains the target device's signed peer_query_device_record through ak.peer.keys.read.lookup.v1 with purpose mls_group_admission, verifies it by the section 8.2 rules, and requires attestation device_authorize_event_id to equal the claim record's and device_signing_key_did to be the key that verified the KeyPackage and LeafNode signatures; the Agent branch keeps its existing Agent signer evidence rule; no producer's control history is ever replayed
the destination-signed claim_receipt is verified over the claim bytes the requester recomputes, not over a reserialization the response supplies

all four checks -- peer device-directory attestation (or Agent signer evidence), claim receipt, KeyPackage signature and every selector -- complete before the KeyPackage is installed and before a Welcome is authored, so a later mismatch cannot be discovered after the group already exists
any one of the eight mutations blocks both installing the KeyPackage and authoring the Welcome; neither is reached on a partial verification
the wire carries no PCR, control-history, device or Agent signer-evidence sidecar, and an external verifier never replays PCR genesis, RealmCommits or complete control history

cases.name: welcome_add_commit_and_claim_record_binding

accepted_winning_add_commit.read_surface: registered accepted Event / RealmCommit / governance dependency read

assertions: the recipient verifies that the signed delivery names the accepted winning Add Commit on the same Genesis lineage
the delivery claim ref resolves one durable claim record whose recipient and endpoint match the accepted Commit and current authorization
a losing or unrelated Commit, changed claim reference or endpoint, or unverified local cache entry rejects before decryption

cases.name: welcome_consume_only_after_durable_group_state
assertions: the recipient durably stores new MLS group state and signs its durable receipt before consuming the exact claim
consume through the owner's Station is idempotent under the original signed request; a response timeout cannot authorize a new claim identity

cases.name: mls_keypackage_actor_and_ciphersuite_closure
assertions: the active registry row 0x0001 is the only v1 suite accepted by publish, claim and Commit submission
each of publish, claim and Commit independently rejects an unknown or reserved suite without a state change
a later active suite in a try-many sequence is not attempted after an unsupported selector and a foreign selector is never rewritten locally
both endpoint KAT branches carry UTF8 RFC 8785/JCS of the complete ActorId in the BasicCredential and the same ActorId is preserved by claim and Welcome

expiry_security_case.evidence_scope: HPKE base-mode X25519/HKDF-SHA256/AES-128-GCM encrypted GroupSecrets layer with MLS EncryptWithLabel context; synthetic encrypted_group_info context. This is not a complete Welcome/group or a live Station expiry test.
